title: Pinterest Step by Step – A Guide to the Platform
excerpt: Pinterest is a visual search engine where a well-built Pin keeps working for months after it goes up. See what Pins, boards, and saves are, how the feed works, who actually uses the platform, and how to put it to work for your brand.
metaDescription: What is Pinterest and how do you use it? Pins, boards, and saves, how the feed and search work, who the users are, Pinterest SEO, and ways to put the platform to work in brand marketing.

runs.text: What is Pinterest?

Pinterest is a platform that works first and foremost as a search engine for visual content. It combines a library of inspiration with the trappings of a social network. People use it to look for ideas and save the things they want to come back to later, and to take part in the community by commenting on them.

Unlike a lot of other platforms, Pinterest gives content a remarkably long life. Pins can be searched for and discovered long after they go up, so a well-built post can keep bringing in traffic for months.

Pinterest also has serious commercial potential. A Pin can send someone straight to a brand’s website or to a specific product page, creating a short path from inspiration to purchase. Better still, people can save a product and return to it later, once they are ready to decide.
What are Pins, boards, and saves?

At its simplest, a Pin is the basic unit of publishing on Pinterest. It can hold a photo, a graphic, or a video, along with a description, a title, and a link out to a website, an article, or a particular product. That way a Pin is not only inspiration — it can also point someone straight to the place where they can learn more or buy.
Because Pinterest is a visual search engine, the image is the critical part of every Pin. You cannot publish text on its own here, so the message always has to travel with a visual.

Saving Pins does exactly what the name suggests: it keeps interesting content for later. Nobody has to decide to buy on the spot — they can hold on to the inspiration and come back to it when the moment suits them.
Pins are saved to boards, a kind of catalog that sorts content by theme. Boards can cover anything — home decor ideas, recipes, travel, outfits. You can also follow other people’s boards.
How do the feed and the search engine work?

Pinterest pairs content search with a recommendation system, so people can both actively hunt for inspiration and stumble on new things while browsing. Type in a specific phrase and you get Pins that match the query.

The home feed matters just as much: it surfaces suggestions tuned to a person’s interests. Pinterest weighs things like past searches, saved Pins, and activity on the platform. Which means the more someone uses it, the better the algorithm reads their interests and picks what comes next.
How do people actually use the platform?

Pinterest may not be as well known as the biggest social networks, but it holds a solid position in Poland, ranking 6th among the most popular platforms. Its community also has a very specific profile — 76% of global users are women.

Gen Z is making its presence felt too, already accounting for 42% of Pinterest’s monthly active users. At the same time, 57% of users are under 35, with 25–34-year-olds the largest group of all. That makes Pinterest a particularly interesting channel for brands trying to reach a younger audience.

There is real potential in the premium and luxury segment as well. For that group, Pinterest is more than a source of inspiration. Statistics show that 3 in 5 luxury shoppers use Pinterest to research brands and products in the category. What is more, 70% of the audience interested in luxury goods is under 35. That makes Pinterest an attractive space for premium brands looking to build interest in their products among young adults.
How is Pinterest different from Instagram?

Instagram, like Pinterest, is built on visual communication — and yet the two platforms are very different animals. Instagram leans heavily on current events, activity, and a steady stream of new posts; Pinterest behaves far more like a search engine. On Instagram, content is usually consumed fast and loses relevance over time. On Pinterest, the same piece can be discovered and viewed again and again, long after it was published.
What does Pinterest SEO look like?

Given how it works, Pinterest leans hard on recognizing images, colors, and the objects inside them, as well as on reading keywords and sorting content into the right categories. It also offers visual search — finding similar images from a single photo — which further supports how published content gets recognized and classified.
How do you use the platform well?

Pinterest gives brands a lot of room to work with, so the key is understanding what someone is looking for and at which moment a given brand or product might interest them. How does that translate into practice? Here are a few ways to put the platform to work:
Build themed boards

Rather than dumping everything in one place, organize it around specific interests. People find what they came for more easily, and the brand gets to show its knowledge and its products in a wider context.
Do not stop at the product

Pinterest works best when the product is part of a bigger idea. A brand selling kitchen equipment can build a board of recipes, quick dinner ideas, or ways to organize a kitchen. The product then turns up while someone is looking to solve a specific problem.
Optimize the Pin itself

A well-made graphic is only the start. Use keywords tied to the topic in the title and description, and point the link straight at the related page, product, or article. That makes the content easier to find and gives people a short route from inspiration to action.
Make Pins that answer real needs

Instead of recycling graphics from other platforms, think about what someone might genuinely be searching for on Pinterest. A clothing brand could skip the “our products” category and build Pins around specific needs instead — “Summer wedding guest outfits,” “What to wear to the office in summer,” or “Ways to style white trousers.” Pins like that keep getting discovered long after they go up.
